title: Voyantra — service overview
description: Read top to bottom: is it healthy, who served it, did it tell the truth, where did the time go, and are the dependencies alive. Every panel here is backed by a metric the app actually emits.

panels.title: 0 — Is the service healthy right now?
panels.description: The six numbers to read first. Anything red here means look at the sections below.

panels.title: Run p50 (NFR < 20s)
panels.description: Median end-to-end itinerary time. NFR target is under 20s. This is the typical experience, not the worst one.

panels.title: Run p95 (NFR < 45s)
panels.description: 95th percentile itinerary time. NFR is 45s. A breach here fires RunLatencyP95Breached after 10m.

panels.title: Cost / itinerary p95 (cap $0.30)
panels.description: 95th percentile spend per itinerary against the $0.30 hard cap. Reading ~0 means the local engine is serving; a jump means a paid venue took over.

panels.title: Runs / sec
panels.description: Completed planner runs per second, all statuses.

panels.title: Failure rate
panels.description: Fraction of runs that did NOT succeed. Degraded-but-honest answers still count as succeeded — see section 2 for those.

panels.title: Spend today (all venues)
panels.description: Cumulative LLM spend since process start. Compare with DAILY_SPEND_LIMIT_USD; the breaker refuses new runs at 100%.

panels.title: 1 — Which venue is actually answering, and what does it cost?
panels.description: One block per serving-chain leg. 'not served since restart' is meaningful: it means the chain never reached that leg, which is what you WANT for the paid ones.

panels.title: local-sglang · latency p50
panels.description: Median seconds per LLM call served by local-sglang. Run duration averages over whichever leg answered and so cannot show this.

panels.title: local-sglang · latency p95
panels.description: 95th percentile call latency on local-sglang. The first call after idle is slower on a local engine (CUDA graph warmup).

panels.title: local-sglang · calls/sec
panels.description: Successful completions per second served by local-sglang.

panels.title: local-sglang · spend
panels.description: Cumulative USD on local-sglang. A self-hosted venue reads exactly $0 — recorded, not absent, so 'free' and 'not measured' cannot be confused.

panels.description: Median seconds per LLM call served by local-vllm. Run duration averages over whichever leg answered and so cannot show this.

panels.description: 95th percentile call latency on groq. The first call after idle is slower on a local engine (CUDA graph warmup).

panels.title: Which venue served, over time
panels.description: Calls per second per venue. The moment a paid leg starts climbing, a free one died — this is the earliest visible symptom of a dead engine.

panels.title: Tokens/sec by venue and direction
panels.description: Throughput split input vs output. Output tokens dominate cost on hosted venues and dominate latency on local ones.

panels.title: 2 — Is the product refusing what it must?
panels.description: A wrong answer and an honest refusal are both HTTP 200. This section separates them.

panels.title: Itinerary outcomes
panels.description: grounded = built from retrieved POIs. degraded = the place exists but retrieval found nothing usable. not_found = geocoding failed and we said so. A rise in degraded with no rise in errors IS silent quality loss.

panels.title: POIs returned per retrieval
panels.description: How much grounding material each query actually got. A p50 falling toward 0 means the corpus or Overpass is failing, and the itineraries above it are being written from far less evidence than they look like they have.

panels.title: Rate limiting by scope
panels.description: Refusals per scope. tenant_min bounds burst, tenant_day is the budget, ip_min closes the cookie-rotation hole. A 429 here is enforcement working, not an outage.

panels.title: API dispatch outcomes
panels.description: queued = accepted. rate_limited = refused by a limit. disabled = the kill switch or spend breaker refused it.

panels.title: 3 — Where does the time actually go?
panels.description: End-to-end latency is a sum. This is the breakdown, so a regression can be attributed instead of guessed at.

panels.title: Stage latency p95
panels.description: Per-stage 95th percentile: geocode -> gather -> compose -> critic. Recorded even when a stage RAISES, so a stage that fails slowly cannot look instantaneous.

panels.title: End-to-end percentiles vs NFR
panels.description: The three NFR percentiles on one axis. Note these mix venues: a local engine and Groq have different physics, so read section 1 alongside.

panels.title: Cache hit rate
panels.description: Hits over hits+misses. 'skipped' is excluded on purpose — those are breaker-open calls that never asked Redis, and counting them as misses would make a Redis outage look like a cold cache.

panels.title: Cache events by tool
panels.description: hit / miss / skipped / error per tool. A rise in 'skipped' means the Redis breaker is open and every lookup is bypassing the cache.

panels.title: Critic corrections
panels.description: How often the critic sent an itinerary back for a rewrite. Zero forever is suspicious — it usually means the critic is not running, not that the model is perfect.

panels.title: 4 — Are the parts underneath still healthy?
panels.description: The dependencies. These fail quietly by design, so they need looking at deliberately.

panels.title: Serving venue circuit breakers
panels.description: 0 = closed (healthy), 1 = half-open (one probe admitted), 2 = open (leg skipped). A venue stuck at 2 is a leg you think you have and do not.

panels.title: Errors by type
panels.description: llm_transient = a leg failed and the chain fell through (normal during failover). llm_timeout = the venue exceeded its budget. llm_non_retryable = OUR bad request, which fails identically everywhere and is never the venue's fault.

panels.title: Runs by status
panels.description: Terminal run states. Compare with section 2: a run can succeed while producing a degraded itinerary.

panels.title: Cumulative spend by venue
panels.description: Money, by venue, since process start. The line that matters is a paid venue climbing while a free one is supposed to be serving.
